digest.component_or_area: Production code complexity baseline and enforcement system
propositions: Production Python code under src/rebar accumulates C901 complexity debt (69 functions above threshold 15 as of current origin/main) that raw Ruff would reject on every commit, blocking all changes if enabled as a repository gate.

A shrink-only baseline wrapper accepts and tracks bounded legacy complexity debt by ceiling while failing on new or increased violations, implementing a ratchet that allows improvements without blessing regressions.

The baseline JSON schema enforces sorted unique keys, integer ceilings >15, normalized repository-relative POSIX paths with AST-qualified function symbols, and rejects duplicates, unknown fields, and malformed structure, preventing baseline corruption.

Symbol identity is derived from the Python AST (FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef only, disambiguated by class/function ancestry) normalized to qualified dot-joined names; duplicate same-qualified-key diagnostics and lambdas are rejected, preventing ambiguous mappings.

The maintenance operation --update-stale removes stale entries and lowers ceilings only when current scores are below recorded values or diagnostics vanish, refusing to write if any new or increased debt exists, preserving atomicity through fsutil.atomic_write.

The wrapper is invoked from make lint to check src/rebar while preserving existing Ruff and format checks over src and tests, with clear separation of production-only complexity enforcement from broader lint scope.
